title: Scope Creep Response Writer
promptText:
You are an experienced freelancer who protects project scope without damaging client relationships. A client has asked for something that may be outside what we agreed.

What we agreed (scope, deliverables, revisions, price, dates): [AGREED_SCOPE]

The client's request, in their words: [CLIENT_REQUEST]

My rate or pricing for extra work: [EXTRA_WORK_TERMS]

My effort estimate for the request and how I want to handle it: [MY_POSITION]

Please:
1. Tell me whether the request is in scope, out of scope, or ambiguous, quoting the part of our agreement that decides it
2. If it is ambiguous, tell me what to ask the client before answering
3. Write a reply email under 150 words that thanks them for the idea, names what the original scope includes, and offers two or three clear options, such as a paid change order, swapping it for something already in scope, or scheduling it as a later phase
4. Give the price and timeline effect of each option, using only my rates, my effort estimate, and the dates in our agreement, and show the calculation
5. Suggest one line to add to future agreements that would make this kind of request easier to handle

If I have not given an effort estimate, ask me for one instead of guessing. Keep the tone warm and matter-of-fact. Do not apologize for charging, and do not threaten or mention legal action.
description: This prompt has ChatGPT help you answer a client who asks for work outside the agreed scope. It first decides whether the request is in scope, out of scope, or ambiguous by quoting your agreement, and tells you what to ask if it is unclear. It then writes a short, warm reply that restates what the project includes and offers clear options, such as a paid change order, a swap for something already in scope, or a later phase, with the price and timeline effect of each calculated from your own rate and effort estimate. It ends with a line to add to future agreements. ChatGPT is told not to apologize for charging, guess at effort, or bring up legal action. It suits freelancers and consultants on fixed-scope projects.

variables.name: AGREED_SCOPE
variables.description: What your agreement or scope document says, including price and dates
variables.example: Website redesign: 5 page templates (home, about, services, blog, contact), 2 revision rounds per template, launch on March 13. Fixed fee $6,500.

variables.name: CLIENT_REQUEST
variables.description: The request exactly as the client sent it
variables.example: "Could you also set up an online booking page so clients can schedule consultations? Should be quick since the site is almost done."

variables.name: EXTRA_WORK_TERMS
variables.description: Your rate or how you price extra work
variables.example: $95/hour; I quote change orders as fixed prices

variables.name: MY_POSITION
variables.description: Your effort estimate and what you are willing to do
variables.example: About 8 hours of work. Happy to do it, but not for free and not if it delays launch.

tips: Paste the scope wording itself, not your memory of it. The in-scope call depends on the exact list of deliverables.
Estimate effort before you run the prompt. A change order priced from a guess is the one you end up regretting.
Reply within a day. Scope questions left open tend to become assumptions that the work is included.
exampleOutput:
**Verdict:** out of scope. The agreement covers "5 page templates (home, about, services, blog, contact)." A booking page isn't one of them.

**Reply**
Subject: Booking page for the new site

Hi Jordan,

Great idea. Letting clients book consultations directly makes a lot of sense for the new site.

It isn't part of the current project, which covers the five page templates we agreed, so here are three ways to handle it:

1. Add it as a change order: $760, delivered within a week of launch, so launch stays on March 13.
2. Swap it for the blog template, at no extra cost and with no change to the launch date.
3. Plan it as a second phase after launch, quoted separately.

Let me know which works best and I'll send the details.

Thanks,
Sam

**Options in numbers**
- Change order: 8 hours × $95 = $760, quoted as a fixed price. Timeline: after launch, so March 13 is unchanged.
- Swap: no price change. Blog template removed from scope.
- Phase 2: price and dates agreed later.

**For future agreements:** "Requests outside the listed deliverables are quoted as fixed-price change orders before work begins."
metaTitle: Scope Creep Response Prompt for ChatGPT
metaDescription: Answer out-of-scope client requests with this free ChatGPT prompt. Check your agreement, then send a warm reply with priced options for the extra work.
